title: 打个电话要等一天
title_en: A Phone Call That Takes a Day

segments.zh: In two weeks, saying hello to Voyager 1
segments.en: 再过两周，跟旅行者一号说声“你好”，

segments.zh: takes a full day to arrive.
Its reply?
Another day. Two days for one hello.
segments.en: 再等一天。一声你好，来回两天。

segments.zh: On November eighteenth,
Voyager 1 reaches one light day from Earth.
segments.en: 旅行者一号离地球一光日。

segments.zh: That is about twenty six billion kilometers,
or sixteen billion miles.
segments.en: 也就是一百六十亿英里。

segments.zh: It made the Hacker News front page this week,
segments.en: 这周它上了 Hacker News 首页，

segments.zh: and everyone is doing the math.
Today's brain teaser:
why does a call take a day, and how do we even hear it?
segments.en: 打个电话凭啥要等一天？我们又是怎么听见的？

segments.zh: Meet our hero, Voyager 1,
launched in nineteen seventy seven.
Forty nine years on the road.
Still talking.
Twist one: the slow part is not Voyager.
segments.en: 反转一：慢的不是旅行者，

segments.zh: It is light.
Light is the fastest thing there is:
three hundred thousand kilometers a second.
Sunlight takes eight minutes to reach us.
segments.en: 太阳光到地球要八分钟，

segments.zh: Moonlight takes about one second.
A radio wave is light too,
so it obeys the same speed limit.
A new phone will not help.
Neither will a better plan.
Voyager itself flies about seventeen kilometers a second.
segments.en: 旅行者自己每秒飞十七公里，

segments.zh: That is sixty thousand kilometers an hour.
Fast?
Light is still about seventeen thousand times faster.
segments.en: 光还是比它快一万七千多倍。

segments.zh: So it took forty nine years
to get one light day away.
Twist two: Voyager whispers.
segments.en: 反转二：旅行者说话像耳语，

segments.zh: Its radio uses about twenty watts.
NASA compares that to a fridge light bulb,
segments.en: NASA 说，差不多一个冰箱灯泡，

segments.zh: shouting across the solar system.
And the farther it goes,
the fainter it gets, fast.
Picture a can of spray paint.
The paint spreads over a bigger and bigger ball.
segments.en: 漆铺在一个越来越大的球面上。

segments.zh: Twice as far,
four times fainter.
So how do we hear it?
With giant ears.
NASA's Deep Space Network
uses dishes seventy meters wide.
One in California, one in Spain, one in Australia,
segments.en: 加州、西班牙、澳大利亚各一处，

segments.zh: so as Earth spins, one always faces deep space.
segments.en: 地球怎么转，总有一个朝着深空。

segments.zh: The dish gathers that whisper
like a bowl catching rain.
Twist three, the most mind bending: one light day sounds far,
segments.en: 反转三，最烧脑：一光日听着很远，

segments.zh: but it is next door.
The nearest star is over four light years away.
segments.en: 最近的恒星在四光年开外，

segments.zh: That is more than fifteen hundred light days.
segments.en: 也就是一千五百多光日。

segments.zh: At Voyager's speed, going that far
segments.en: 按旅行者的速度飞过去，

segments.zh: would take about seventy five thousand years, by our math.
segments.en: 我们算了算，要七万五千年。

segments.zh: And Voyager is not even aimed at that star.
segments.en: 而且它根本不是朝那颗星飞的，

segments.zh: It is just drifting through the dark.
In twenty twelve it left the Sun's bubble,
segments.en: 二零一二年，它飞出了太阳的“泡泡”，

segments.zh: the first spacecraft ever to do it.
Its power keeps fading,
so NASA keeps switching instruments off.
segments.en: NASA 只能一台台关掉仪器。

segments.zh: In April twenty twenty six, one more went quiet,
segments.en: 二零二六年四月，又关掉一台，

segments.zh: to save energy.
Fine print: the date and distance come from EarthSky, using NASA data.
segments.en: 友情提示：日期和距离来自 EarthSky 根据 NASA 的数据；

segments.zh: Seventy five thousand years is our own math on paper.
segments.en: 七万五千年是我们在纸上算的。

segments.zh: Voyager 2 is behind it.
It reaches one light day around twenty thirty five.
segments.en: 大约二零三五年到一光日。

segments.zh: So why does the call take a day?
segments.en: 所以电话凭啥要等一天？

segments.zh: Because even light needs a day to get there.
And how do we hear it?
With giant ears, and a lot of patience.
Next time a text feels slow,
think of Voyager. It waits a whole day, and still says hello.
segments.en: 想想旅行者：等一天，还在说你好。
